_comment: Which reply leads to which line. The one thing about an NPC the client has never held.
The client ships every line an NPC can say and every reply it can be given, and nowhere does
it say which goes with which - measured across all 6,467 of them. That pairing has always
lived on Ankama's server, so it cannot be extracted or measured. It has to be decided, and
this is where the decision goes.
npc         the NPC's id
map         0 for wherever it stands; a map id to say something different there
opening     which line it starts on; the first one when left out
lines       one per thing it says, each with what can be said back
next        the line that reply leads to; left out, the conversation ends
And what a reply is FOR, which is what stops a conversation offering everything at once:
startsQuest  this reply hands that quest over. Not the same as `quest`: this one is how a
quest begins, so it is offered to somebody who has NOT got it.
quest        only offered while that quest is under way.
step         and only while it is on that step.
afterQuest   only offered once the quest is finished.
{ "npc": 1088, "map": 0, "opening": 3312, "lines": [
{ "message": 6047, "choices": [ { "reply": 7846 } ] } ] }
A line with no replies is fine now: the client draws its own Leave button and the X closes the
window, because the server answers the kla it sends. It did not before, which is why an NPC
with nothing to say back used to trap you in the conversation.
WHERE THESE COME FROM. The ids are the client's own. The wiring - which reply leads where -
is read off the walkthroughs at dofuspourlesnoobs, which write the reply options out in
French, and matched back to ids with tools/dialogue_from_guide.py. Inside one NPC the text
identifies its lines 98.3% of the time, and the reply ids do not have to be Ankama's: the
server sends the ids and the client sends back what it was given, so any id with the right
text works as long as the tree agrees with itself.

dialogues._note2: «Consejo de clase» (2009). The guide gives it to the Conseillere Archie at [4,-19] with the requirement «On marche sur des oeufs», which is our 1959. Its step 2631 carries dialogId 0, so there is NO measured hand-over line: it hangs off her opening line with reply 36990 «Demander la raison de sa convocation», which is the only one of her 59 that talks about a summons and fits a class council. The reconstruction is ours; the requirement and the NPC are the guide's.

dialogues._note: «He visto el anuncio que has puesto» requires having clicked 489412, the tavern building on the outdoor map 153878787. The guide says «Cliquez pour accepter l offre», and the element carries the SAME id on the two adjacent maps [0,-3] and [1,-3], which is what a building that spans both does. It is the oddest one on the map that is not the door: the other two candidates were discarded because 32613 is the phoenix rocks and 42509 is the entrance door.
